figures.name: Prototype cost crossover for repeated credential verification
figures.alt: Cumulative and per-check prototype costs compare graph proofs, fresh envelope-to-graph expansion and an envelope-only check with a trusted cached mapping.
figures.description: Cumulative and per-check prototype costs compare graph proofs, fresh envelope-to-graph expansion and an envelope-only check with a trusted cached mapping.
figures.caption: Cost model using run-3 prototype timings for IRI-only credentials on one thread. (a) The curves sum median batch means for issuance, ingestion and R re-verifications of a 146-quad credential. The calculated crossover is R*=4.24 for the envelope path with fresh expansion: at that point both paths have accumulated about 6.1 ms; left of it B costs less because its issuance and ingestion are cheaper, right of it A costs less because each further check costs 0.28 ms in A and 1.06 ms in B, so that at R=10 B has cost 1.6 times A. The dashed envelope-only curve excludes checks on a cached RDF view. (b) Measured A1, B1 and B1s by credential size. The crossover labels use B1 and include issuance.

figures.name: Qualified authority and content assurance remain distinct
figures.alt: Qualified authority checks do not eliminate a feasible independent attack on an ordinary content declaration that changes the accepted outcome.
figures.description: Qualified authority checks do not eliminate a feasible independent attack on an ordinary content declaration that changes the accepted outcome.
figures.caption: An illustrative policy under A2. (a) An authority edge validated at E bounds the decision by K(E) if it is a single direct attack target satisfying T3(c). (b) If graph-profile issuance and validation make those edges Q, an E declaration that can independently change the accepted outcome still bounds the decision. Equality requires a matching lower bound from T3(a).

figures.name: How a machine verifies and unnests an industrial credential
figures.alt: Side-by-side steps compare stored graph-proof verification with envelope-only B1 processing, disclosure reconstruction, expansion and source binding.
figures.description: Side-by-side steps compare stored graph-proof verification with envelope-only B1 processing, disclosure reconstruction, expansion and source binding.
figures.caption: A machine checking the same stored battery claim through A and envelope-only B1. The dual-proof nested example in Appendix A additionally verifies the inner graph proof. Unnesting includes authentication, disclosure reconstruction and controlled interpretation; decoding alone proves nothing. The displayed timings cover prototype portions of the process, not all steps or complete security checks. A cached mapping can replace fresh expansion only under a policy protecting its source binding, freshness and status.
